walkthrough:
Identify and describe the two transformations mapping $y = f(x)$ to $y = f(2x) - 3$:
1. Stretch with scale factor $\frac{1}{2}$ in the $x$-direction (parallel to the $x$-axis).
2. Translation by vector $\begin{pmatrix}0\\-3\end{pmatrix}$ (or $3$ units vertically downwards in the negative $y$-direction).

hints: Set the transformed coordinates equal to $(5, 6)$: $2x_{\text{orig}} = 5$ and $y_{\text{orig}} - 3 = 6$.
walkthrough:
Reverse the transformations applied to the point $P(5, 6)$ on $y = f(2x) - 3$:
$$x_{\text{trans}} = 2x_{\text{orig}} = 5 \implies x_{\text{orig}} = 10$$
$$y_{\text{trans}} = y_{\text{orig}} - 3 = 6 \implies y_{\text{orig}} = 6 + 3 = 9$$
Thus, the original coordinates are $(10, 9)$.
